title: The Girl Who Taught a Drone to See

pages.text: On Saturdays near Techiman in the Bono East Region, fourteen-year-old Mansa walked with her Uncle Kwabena through his five-hectare maize farm. By the time Uncle Kwabena noticed yellow streaks and chewed leaves in the middle rows, pests and plant disease had already damaged a third of that section. ‘A farmer cannot inspect ten thousand maize plants leaf by leaf every single morning,’ Uncle Kwabena sighed.
sentences: On Saturdays near Techiman in the Bono East Region, fourteen-year-old Mansa walked with her Uncle Kwabena through his five-hectare maize farm.
By the time Uncle Kwabena noticed yellow streaks and chewed leaves in the middle rows, pests and plant disease had already damaged a third of that section.
‘A farmer cannot inspect ten thousand maize plants leaf by leaf every single morning,’ Uncle Kwabena sighed.
pages.alt: Fourteen-year-old Mansa and Uncle Kwabena inspect yellowing maize leaves in a large green maize field near Techiman.

pages.text: At Monday’s JHS coding and robotics club, Mansa shared an idea with her teammate Tariq. ‘What if we attach a small camera to the club’s quadcopter drone and train an artificial intelligence, an AI computer vision programme, to spot sick maize leaves from the air?’ Tariq’s eyes lit up. ‘Instead of following fixed rules written by hand, a machine-learning model learns patterns from hundreds of example images called training data!’
sentences: At Monday’s JHS coding and robotics club, Mansa shared an idea with her teammate Tariq.
‘What if we attach a small camera to the club’s quadcopter drone and train an artificial intelligence, an AI computer vision programme, to spot sick maize leaves from the air?’ Tariq’s eyes lit up.
‘Instead of following fixed rules written by hand, a machine-learning model learns patterns from hundreds of example images called training data!’
pages.alt: In a JHS computer lab, Mansa and Tariq examine a small camera drone and a laptop screen showing healthy and diseased leaf photos.

pages.text: Eager to move fast, Mansa and Tariq downloaded 500 photographs of maize leaves from an online agricultural website, 250 labelled Healthy and 250 labelled Diseased. Every photo had been taken indoors against a plain white background under bright studio lamps. When they tested their model on 100 similar studio photos, it scored 90 correct out of 100, a 90 percent accuracy rate! They thought their invention was ready.
sentences: Eager to move fast, Mansa and Tariq downloaded 500 photographs of maize leaves from an online agricultural website, 250 labelled Healthy and 250 labelled Diseased.
Every photo had been taken indoors against a plain white background under bright studio lamps.
When they tested their model on 100 similar studio photos, it scored 90 correct out of 100, a 90 percent accuracy rate!
They thought their invention was ready.
pages.alt: Mansa and Tariq celebrate in the computer lab as their laptop screen shows a green progress bar for studio leaf photos.

pages.text: On Saturday morning, District Agricultural Extension Officer Madam Amina joined them at Uncle Kwabena’s farm for their first real field trial. The sky was overcast, red Harmattan dust coated the lower maize leaves, and morning dew cast dark shadows across the rows. Tariq flew the small drone along 20 marked farm plots while Mansa’s tablet analysed the camera images.
sentences: On Saturday morning, District Agricultural Extension Officer Madam Amina joined them at Uncle Kwabena’s farm for their first real field trial.
The sky was overcast, red Harmattan dust coated the lower maize leaves, and morning dew cast dark shadows across the rows.
Tariq flew the small drone along 20 marked farm plots while Mansa’s tablet analysed the camera images.
pages.alt: Under a cloudy morning sky at the maize farm, Tariq pilots the small drone over dusty maize rows while Madam Amina, Uncle Kwabena and Mansa watch.

pages.text: The field results were a shock! Out of 20 farm plots, the AI got only 9 right and misclassified 11, an accuracy of just 45 percent! Worse still, the app sounded a red alarm on 8 completely healthy plots coated in harmless red laterite dust, calling them severely diseased, while missing 3 shaded plots that actually had early leaf blight. ‘Why did a 90-percent model fail on a real farm?’ Mansa asked in dismay.
sentences: The field results were a shock!
Out of 20 farm plots, the AI got only 9 right and misclassified 11, an accuracy of just 45 percent!

Worse still, the app sounded a red alarm on 8 completely healthy plots coated in harmless red laterite dust, calling them severely diseased, while missing 3 shaded plots that actually had early leaf blight.
‘Why did a 90-percent model fail on a real farm?’ Mansa asked in dismay.
pages.alt: Mansa looks dismayed at her tablet screen while Madam Amina uses a magnifying hand lens to show that a dusty maize leaf is actually healthy.

pages.text: Madam Amina knelt beside a maize plant and wiped the red dust from a leaf. ‘Your model suffered from training-data bias,’ she explained kindly. ‘Because it only saw studio photos on white paper, it never learned what Ghanaian maize looks like in cloudy light, wind, weeds or red soil. It mistook red dust for leaf disease, a false positive, and missed real disease hiding in shadows, a false negative!’

It mistook red dust for leaf disease, a false positive, and missed real disease hiding in shadows, a false negative!’
pages.alt: Madam Amina wipes red soil dust off a healthy green maize leaf to show Mansa and Tariq why the camera was confused.

pages.text: Before they took a single new photograph, Madam Amina taught them another essential rule of responsible technology: privacy and informed consent. ‘A drone camera flies high enough to see neighbouring compounds, workers and farm boundaries,’ she said. ‘Never fly over people’s homes, never record faces or private property without permission, and always explain to farmers how their farm data will be stored and used.’
sentences: Before they took a single new photograph, Madam Amina taught them another essential rule of responsible technology: privacy and informed consent.
‘A drone camera flies high enough to see neighbouring compounds, workers and farm boundaries,’ she said.
‘Never fly over people’s homes, never record faces or private property without permission, and always explain to farmers how their farm data will be stored and used.’
pages.alt: Madam Amina, Mansa and Tariq review a farm map with Uncle Kwabena and neighbouring farmers to agree on flight boundaries and consent.

pages.text: Over the next six months, Mansa, Tariq and their club worked the scientific way. With written permission from twelve local farmers, they walked the fields alongside Madam Amina. For every photograph, Madam Amina inspected the real plant with her hand lens so the label was scientifically verified. Together they built a balanced Ghanaian dataset of 2,000 leaf images across sunny, cloudy, dusty and rainy conditions.
sentences: Over the next six months, Mansa, Tariq and their club worked the scientific way.

Together they built a balanced Ghanaian dataset of 2,000 leaf images across sunny, cloudy, dusty and rainy conditions.
pages.alt: Mansa photographs maize leaves with a camera while Madam Amina inspects the leaves with a hand lens to verify each label.

pages.text: Before testing the new model, Mansa split their 2,000 verified images carefully: 1,800 images were used as training data to teach the model, while 200 completely unseen images from different farm plots were locked away as a separate test set. ‘If you test an AI on the exact same pictures it studied,’ Tariq noted, ‘that is like giving a student the exam questions before the test!’
sentences: Before testing the new model, Mansa split their 2,000 verified images carefully: 1,800 images were used as training data to teach the model, while 200 completely unseen images from different farm plots were locked away as a separate test set.
‘If you test an AI on the exact same pictures it studied,’ Tariq noted, ‘that is like giving a student the exam questions before the test!’
pages.alt: In the school lab, Mansa and Tariq separate their dataset on screen into a large training group and a locked test group.

pages.text: When they ran the retrained model on the 200 unseen Ghanaian field images, it classified 180 correctly, a true field accuracy of 90 percent! Even more importantly, Mansa redesigned the app so it never claimed to be infallible. Instead of telling farmers to spray chemicals immediately, the app created a map of flagged rows for the farmer and an agricultural extension officer to inspect in person.

pages.alt: Uncle Kwabena and Madam Amina use Mansa’s tablet map to walk directly to a flagged row of maize plants for a close human check.

pages.text: By the following harvest, Uncle Kwabena and his neighbours spotted early armyworm and leaf blight weeks sooner, saving crops and reducing unnecessary pesticide spraying. When Mansa’s team won the regional young innovators’ prize, she credited the farmers and Madam Amina. ‘AI is a powerful tool,’ Mansa said, ‘but it works only when paired with honest data, ethical rules and human wisdom.’

pages.alt: At a regional science fair, Mansa and Tariq share the stage with Uncle Kwabena and Madam Amina beside their agricultural drone.

pages.text: Back in the coding club, Mansa wrote on the whiteboard: What Would You Build, Discover or Change? ‘One day we want to grow this into an African agritech company serving farmers across the continent,’ she told her teammates, ‘starting with careful experiments right here at home.’ What problem in your school, farm or town could technology and human teamwork help solve together?

activities.question: Why did Mansa’s first AI model drop from 90% accuracy in the studio to 45% (9 out of 20) on Uncle Kwabena’s farm?
options: It trained only on studio photos, so red dust and shadows confused it
The drone flew too high into outer space
Maize plants change into cocoa trees on Saturdays
activities.explanation: Training-data bias occurred because the studio dataset did not represent real Ghanaian field conditions like red laterite dust, clouds and shadows.

activities.definition: A systematic error in a computer model caused by training data that does not fairly represent real-world conditions
distractors: The battery cable that connects a drone to a charger
A type of fertiliser used on maize farms

activities.question: Why did Mansa keep 200 verified field images separate from the 1,800 training images?
options: To test honestly how well the AI performs on new, unseen farm images
Because the laptop screen could only hold 1,800 pictures
To delete all healthy maize plants from the farm
activities.explanation: Evaluating a model requires an independent test set of unseen examples; when it got 180 of 200 right, that proved 90% real-world accuracy.

activities.question: Why did Mansa design the app to flag suspicious rows for human inspection instead of ordering automatic chemical spraying?
options: AI can make mistakes, so farmers and experts must verify before acting
Because drones are afraid of maize leaves
Because farmers never need to look at their crops
activities.explanation: Human oversight ("human-in-the-loop") prevents false alarms from wasting money or spraying unnecessary pesticides.

activities.prompt: Order the steps of building a responsible agricultural AI system.
items: Obtain informed consent from farmers and respect privacy boundaries.
Collect diverse real-world field data verified by agricultural experts.
Test the model on unseen field images and keep human experts in the loop.

activities.prompt: How did Mansa and Tariq turn an embarrassing 45% field failure into a stronger invention?

glossary.definition: Made by humans rather than occurring naturally; artificial intelligence is software that performs tasks requiring pattern recognition or learning
A distortion or unfair skew in data or results when training examples leave out real-world conditions
Permission given freely after a person has been clearly informed about what will happen and how their data will be used
A structured collection of data, such as labelled photographs, used to train and test a computer model
